Scheduled report generation with Celery and Celery Beat, and built a Flask and Vue.js admin interface with Cognito login to manage clients and report runs, deployed on EC2 with Docker Compose
Designed and built a data lake for a client's financial analysis with S3, Glue, Athena, Lambda, and Pandas, with QuickSight dashboards and the infrastructure defined in CloudFormation

Operated client workloads migrated to AWS (EC2, RDS, load balancers) and resolved their support tickets through Zendesk: networking, IAM permissions, security group and port changes

Wrote and optimized the reporting queries, both SQL on PostgreSQL and data reads on Bigtable

headline: Go microservices assessment for a life sciences quality management SaaS company
projectDescription: Quality management system (QMS) SaaS for life sciences companies, built as Go microservices on AWS and Kubernetes.
responsibilities: Assessed the client's Go microservices monorepo (architecture, security, performance, and quality assurance) through interview sessions with the team and a review of the codebase
Reviewed the CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions, Argo CD, Trivy, Dependabot) and the ongoing rework from per-customer stacks to a multi-tenant architecture
Identified security gaps: static API keys without granular authorization, secrets kept in environment variables, and no Go-specific security scanning
Identified observability gaps: no distributed tracing or profiling beyond Datadog, and no load testing

Wrote the assessment report with prioritized recommendations and a 0–6 month roadmap: repository interfaces and hexagonal architecture, centralized secret management, gosec and govulncheck in CI, OpenTelemetry tracing, pprof profiling, k6 load testing, and SLOs
results: Delivered the assessment report with a prioritized remediation roadmap
